subject: Estimation of male roe deer density - model mK 'site transient response'

messages.author: b6ebbabd9b16dd3f
messages.subject: Estimation of male roe deer density - model mK 'site transient response'
parts:
Dear secr community,

We are doing a study to estimate the density of male roe deer in 1km2 of forest using 20 photo traps.  The data were analysed using secr and different predefined models on the baseline encounter probability (g0) were tested while keeping the movement parameter σ constant and constant values of the animal density D. Models were compared using the Akaike information criterion (AIC). 

Model selection reveals substantial evidence for the ‘site transient response’ model MK. 

I can't really understand what this MK model means...? 

Does it mean that the efficiency of the site depends on a previous capture? 

Maybe someone could help me to understand a little bit better what this mK model is and what it represents at the biological (applied) level?

Thanks,

Best regards,

Inès

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Estimation of male roe deer density - model mK 'site transient response'
parts:
The vignette secr-overview.pdf defines the predictors 'k' and 'K' as follows
k -  site effectiveness changes once any animal caught
K - site effectiveness depends on preceding occasion

I don't know of any real life application. Perhaps odour may linger in a trap affecting the later probability of catching any animal (though you might think self-odour and other-odour would have different effects). I can't imagine an application to automatic cameras, and if that model is the best by AIC I would suspect it is just a surrogate for some other heterogeneity.
Murray
